items.name: Phagia Canister
items.purpose: Booter’s attached living-algae reserve, carried for eating, drinking and treating injuries. The canister holds the survival supply rather than creating a separate meal or drink each time it is used; its existing attachment and reserve rules still apply.

items.name: Raw Ironstone ore
items.purpose: Bulk iron-bearing rock gathered from exposed Ironstone deposits. It feeds the dry-sorting process, which separates several material fractions; it is raw mineral cargo rather than ready-to-use metal.

items.name: Consolidated iron bar stock
items.purpose: Worked iron consolidated into unfitted bars for fasteners, tool bodies and structural fittings. It is the metal-working stage after an iron bloom or selected ore has been processed, rather than another grade of loose ore. Final section, grade and forging conditions remain to be chosen.

items.name: Shell husks / shed plates
items.purpose: Cheap raw shell/husk material; source of scraped fibers and candidate basic casing/guards. It provides candidate material or a shaped starting piece for making other objects, with the final form set by the receiving design.

items.name: Bone multi-tool shaft
items.purpose: A full-length shaped stone-bone shaft for the two-handed T0 or T1 multi-tool. It provides the head seat and long handhold; the T1 variant captures textured gripping-pad scales between its fitted end hardware.

items.name: Shell tool butt cap
items.purpose: A rounded shell cap covering the butt end of the full-length stone-bone shaft on the T0 and T1 multi-tools. It finishes the rear palm-contact surface and protects the shaft end.

items.name: Iron tool retaining pin
items.purpose: A fitted iron pin securing a digging head and bone shaft through their aligned retaining holes. It is distinct from a Legger pivot pin.

items.name: Forged iron digging head
items.purpose: A full-size transverse forged iron head combining a downturned broad hoe/adze-like digging blade and an opposite rough blunt hammer poll. It mounts on the T1 stone-bone shaft for shallow digging, prying and crude hammering.

items.name: Iron tool head collar
items.purpose: A fitted iron reinforcing collar around the T1 multi-tool or T2 multi-tool head connection. Tool-specific forms are separate fit variants.

items.name: Unconsolidated iron bloom
items.purpose: A rough mass of iron-bearing metal from the proposed smelting stage, awaiting consolidation into usable working stock. It precedes the consolidated iron bars and steel-making branches. Metal yield, entrained residue and the required working process remain unqualified.

items.name: Stone bone
items.purpose: An extremely hard bone that occurs in some fauna. A selected sound length can supply the base material for a fitted bone multi-tool shaft; source selection and shaping still require design.

items.name: Faunal gripping-pad scales
items.purpose: Candidate textured feed for tool grips, foot-contact surfaces and cargo-rest friction pads. It provides candidate material or a shaped starting piece for making other objects, with the final form set by the receiving design.

items.name: Iron-headed multi-tool
items.purpose: A full-length, two-handed iron-headed multi-tool with a transverse dual-ended head: a broad downturned hoe/adze-like digging blade on one side and a rough blunt iron hammer poll on the other. Its stone-bone shaft, reinforcing iron collar, shell butt cap, iron retaining pin and captured gripping-pad scales make a more effective prying and shallow-digging tool than the bone version.

items.name: Bone salvage multi-tool
items.purpose: A full-length, two-handed bone salvage multi-tool with a broad wedge-shaped jawbone head on a stone-bone shaft. The wedge loosens shallow ground and pries salvage; the thick hard bony poll on its opposite side provides crude light hammering. A fitted shell collar, shell butt cap and iron retaining pin hold the simple build together.

items.name: Utility harness
items.purpose: A simple waist harness belt with two attachment mounts. Supports the Personal Phagia canister and the dust harvester canister in this loadout.

stations.name: Workbench
stations.purpose: General camp work surface for fitting parts, assembling tools and repairing ordinary gear. The existing Camp Loop trial uses its workbench to craft an empty Arc Battery; this catalog entry does not expand the trial recipe roster.

stations.name: Dust refinery
stations.purpose: Refine collected Arc Dust into Arc Energy and charge an existing empty Arc Battery. Accept a dust canister and an empty battery, retain the canister and unused dust, and return the same battery charged; dust alone does not create a battery casing.

stations.name: Ironstone refinery
stations.purpose: Camp facility for breaking down and separating raw Ironstone Ore into coarse aggregate, iron-rich concentrate, mineral sand and mineral dust. Represents the existing manual Ironstone sorter; further refining or smelting would require separately designed operations.

stations.name: Cooking station
stations.purpose: Prepare food at camp. Ingredients, preparation, heat and atmosphere requirements are still to be designed.

stations.name: Ceramic forming bench
stations.purpose: Prepare and shape qualified ceramic feed into unfired vessels, molds or fitted blanks before drying and kiln firing. Complements the existing firing kiln; binder chemistry, usable process liquids and feed suitability must be selected explicitly.

stations.name: Contained chemical processing station
stations.purpose: Process separately contained faunal and mineral feedstocks into candidate industrial binders, sealants, lubricants or other processing agents. Select compatible vessels and a qualified process for each product; keep industrial chemicals separate from Phagia and food equipment.

stations.name: Controlled-heating firing kiln
stations.purpose: Candidate stationary kiln. Qualified external power, thermal controls and atmosphere management remain unresolved.

stations.name: Forge hearth
stations.purpose: Proposed bounded workshop heat source for bringing metal to a workable state. It supports a controlled metalworking operation; the workpiece, heat source and suitable supporting tools must be established for the process.

stations.name: Husk processing table
stations.purpose: Hold shell husks and shed plates for scraping chitin/icore fibers and sorting useful shell pieces. Supplies candidate fiber feed for husk paper and later pressing; cheap raw shell does not imply cheap finished textiles.

stations.name: Husk-fiber press
stations.purpose: Press prepared husk-fiber feed into candidate paper sheets or difficult dense fiber stock using process-specific tooling. Paper and garment-grade material remain separate processes; pressing alone does not supply ordinary cloth or bypass costly textile preparation.

stations.name: Legger service stand
stations.purpose: Support accessible Legger assemblies during inspection, cleaning, lubrication and replacement of compatible mechanical parts. Requires the Legger's physical presence and appropriate tools; service outcomes depend on parts and access rather than automatic full repair.

stations.name: Salvage dismantling bench
stations.purpose: Secure recovered scrap and damaged mechanisms for inspection and careful disassembly. Candidate outputs are sorted scrap and individually qualified reusable parts; dismantling does not guarantee repair or reproduce ancient technology.

quantityStatus: provisional unit quantities for the scoped runtime trial; not catalog canon
